newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged mixed, from 0.150 cent per lb higher to 0.150 lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.200 higher, livestock analysts said.
Some analysts expect technical strength again in live cattle futures. Futures held chart support and finished strong. Active feedlot and boxed beef movement may also encourage support, they said.

However, other analysts see cash prices declining further and look for futures to drift lower. Packers will also have more contract cattle available next week once the first of the month arrives, they added.

Feeder cattle futures were expected steady to firmer following another advance in the CME feeder cattle index and expectations for a continued weak corn futures market. Demand for cash feeders is expected to remain strong for the foreseeable future as tight feeder supplies will continue into the fall, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.19 at $78.34 per cwt, a new high for the move and highest level since August 18, 1994.
